@damdo: This pull request explicitly references no jira issue.

<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-api-provider-gcp/pull/292):

>Bumps `manifests-gen` to include webhook namespace scoping, which adds a `namespaceSelector` to all provider webhooks restricting them to the `openshift-cluster-api` namespace.
>
>This prevents webhooks from intercepting requests in other namespaces, which would fail on unsupported platforms where the webhook server is not running.

</details>

--- ## Walkthrough This PR adds namespace-scoped admission control restrictions to GCP-related webhook configurations in the cluster API operator manifests, limiting them to the `openshift-cluster-api` namespace, and updates the supporting manifests-gen dependency version. ## Changes **Webhook Namespace Restriction** | Layer / File(s) | Summary | |---|---| | **Dependency Update**
`openshift/tools/go.mod` | `manifests-gen` dependency version bumped from `v0.0.0-20260429150927-40757eb5602c` to `v0.0.0-20260506082208-390a5b10a37c`. | | **Webhook Configuration**
`openshift/capi-operator-manifests/default/manifests.yaml` | All GCP-related MutatingWebhookConfiguration and ValidatingWebhookConfiguration webhook entries (default/validation prefixes for gcpcluster, gcpclustertemplate, gcpmachine, gcpmachinetemplate; and m/v prefixes for gcpmanagedcluster, gcpmanagedcontrolplane, gcpmanagedcontrolplanetemplate, gcpmanagedmachinepool, gcpmanagedmachinepooltemplate) now include a `namespaceSelector` with `matchLabels { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: openshift-cluster-api }` to restrict webhook interception to the specified namespace. | ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 2 (Simple) | ⏱️ ~12 minutes
